help.title: Help
help.lead: How booking works, what happens when plans change, and how to reach a person.
faq.title: Common questions
faq.p1: Do I need an account to book? Yes. A booking has to belong to somebody, or you could not find it again, change it, or cancel it. Creating one takes an email address and a password.
faq.p2: When am I charged? Once, when you reserve. The total you see on the listing is the total you are charged — there is no booking fee, no facility fee and no currency mark-up added at the payment step.
faq.p3: Why are prices in different currencies? Because each property is priced in its own, and we never convert. A price quoted in one currency and charged in another is a broken promise, not a rounding.
faq.p4: Why do some listings show no photograph? Because the host has not added one yet. We will not fill the gap with a stock photograph of a different building — that would be a false statement about the property you are being asked to pay for.
cancellation.title: Cancelling a booking
cancellation.p1: You can cancel from My bookings at any time. The dates go straight back on sale, so the host is not left with an empty room they did not know about.
cancellation.p2: Refunds are returned to the card you paid with. Where a host has already been paid, we recover their share rather than absorbing it quietly — the money comes back from where it went.
cancellation.p3: A host's own cancellation policy, where they set one, is shown on the listing before you book. If a property is not as advertised, tell us before the stay ends: your money is held until then, which is what gives us something to put right.
safety.title: Safety & reporting
safety.p1: If something is wrong with a property, or somebody has behaved badly, report it. The fastest route is the contact address below with your booking reference — that lets us see the same thing you are looking at.
safety.p2: If you are in immediate danger, contact your local emergency services first. We are a marketplace, not an emergency service, and pretending otherwise would waste time you may not have.
safety.p3: Listings that misrepresent a property are taken down. A verification badge on a listing means a specific check was made and says which; the absence of one means no check has been made, not that a property is unsafe.
contact.title: Contact us
contact.p1: Email support@paltas.io. Include your booking reference if you have one — it is the fastest way for us to find the booking you mean.
contact.p2: We are a small team and we answer in the order things arrive. If a stay is in progress and something is wrong, say so in the first line and it goes to the front.
about.title: About PALTAS
about.lead: One place to find somewhere to stay, rent, buy or sell — with the price stated in full and the checks stated plainly.
how.title: How it works
how.p1: Find a property, choose your dates, and pay once. Your dates are checked again as you reserve, so if somebody took the last room while you were deciding you are told here and not charged.
how.p2: Your money is held after you pay and released to the host after your stay finishes. That gap is deliberate: it is what gives you somewhere to stand if the property is not what was advertised.
how.p3: Hosts, landlords, agents and hotels use the same platform from the other side — to list, to price, to manage staff and to be paid. It is one system, not a shopfront bolted onto a separate back office.
pricing.title: Our pricing promise
pricing.p1: The total on the listing is the total you pay. No booking fee, no facility fee, no currency mark-up, and no line added at the payment step.
pricing.p2: Our own commission is a named line in the breakdown rather than folded into the nightly rate. A marketplace that hides its margin inside the headline price is not being transparent, it is being quiet.
pricing.p3: Prices are shown in each property's own currency and are never converted. Where tax applies, it is collected and remitted rather than added as a surprise.
trust.title: Trust & verification
trust.p1: A badge on a listing means a specific check was made, and it says which: an identity matched to the account holder, a title deed proving the right to let, a property visited in person, a licence on file, payouts confirmed to a named bank account.
trust.p2: Where no check has been made, no badge appears. We would rather show you less than tell you something we have not verified — a badge nobody can interrogate stops reassuring anyone the first time a booking goes wrong.
trust.p3: The same applies to reviews and ratings. A property with no reviews shows no rating, because inventing one is worse than admitting there is nothing to say yet.
verification.title: How verification works
verification.p1: Verification is a check we perform, not a status a host can claim. Each kind is recorded separately with the method used and the month it was done, and the listing shows all three so you can judge it yourself.
verification.p2: It is being rolled out rather than finished. Most listings today carry no badges at all, and that is what the absence of a badge means — no check yet, not a failed one.
languages.title: Languages & currencies
languages.p1: PALTAS reads in fifteen languages, including Arabic and Urdu right-to-left. Your language and the country you are browsing are separate choices, so you can read in Swedish while looking at property in Kenya.
languages.p2: Prices stay in each property's own currency whichever language you read in. Translating a price is a matter of formatting; converting one is a matter of money, and we do not do it.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: What we collect, why, who sees it, and what you can ask us to do with it.
privacy.collect.title: What we collect
privacy.collect.p1: Your name and email address when you create an account; your bookings, the dates and the properties; and messages you send us about them. If you are a host, the property details you publish and the bank account your payouts go to.
privacy.collect.p2: We do not hold your card number. Card details go directly to Stripe, our payment processor, and never reach our servers — we store only Stripe's reference for the payment.
privacy.collect.p3: We record which language and country you have chosen, in a cookie, so the site is in the right language next time. That is a preference, not an identity.
privacy.use.title: What we use it for
privacy.use.p1: Running your bookings: confirming them, showing them to the host who has to let you in, cancelling and refunding them. Answering you when you write to us. Meeting our legal and tax obligations.
privacy.use.p2: We do not sell your data, and we do not share it with advertisers.
privacy.share.title: Who else sees it
privacy.share.p1: The host of a property you book sees what they need to receive you: your name, your dates and your booking reference. They do not see your other bookings or your payment details.
privacy.share.p2: Stripe processes payments and holds the card details we never see. Our hosting and database providers hold the data at rest. Each is bound by contract to use it only to provide that service.
privacy.share.p3: We disclose data to authorities only where the law requires it.
privacy.rights.title: What you can ask for
privacy.rights.p1: A copy of what we hold about you, a correction to anything wrong, or deletion of your account. Write to privacy@paltas.io and we will answer within thirty days.
privacy.rights.p2: Some records survive an account deletion because the law requires it — a completed booking is also a financial record, and we keep those for as long as tax rules oblige us to.
terms.title: Terms
terms.lead: The terms on which PALTAS may be used, by guests and by hosts.
terms.using.title: Using PALTAS
terms.using.p1: You need an account to book, and the details on it must be true. One account belongs to one person; do not share it or let somebody else book on it as though they were you.
terms.using.p2: Do not use PALTAS to advertise a property you have no right to let or sell, or to arrange anything unlawful where the property is.
terms.booking.title: Bookings and payment
terms.booking.p1: A booking is a contract between you and the host. PALTAS operates the marketplace, takes the payment and holds it — it is not itself the host, and does not own or manage the properties listed on it.
terms.booking.p2: The total shown is the total charged. We take a commission from the host, which is stated as its own line, and we add nothing to your side at the payment step.
terms.booking.p3: Cancellations follow the policy shown on the listing at the time you booked. Where we hold money that has not yet reached the host, a refund returns it; where it has, we recover it from the host.
terms.hosting.title: Hosting on PALTAS
terms.hosting.p1: A listing must describe the property accurately, including its photographs. Advertising a property with pictures of a different one is grounds for removal.
terms.hosting.p2: You must have the right to let or sell what you list, and must comply with the tenancy, licensing and tax rules where the property is. Those rules differ by country and they are yours to meet.
terms.hosting.p3: Payouts are made to a verified account after the guest's stay finishes. We may withhold a payout while a dispute about that stay is open.
terms.liability.title: Liability
terms.liability.p1: PALTAS is responsible for operating the platform, taking payment correctly and paying hosts what they are owed. It is not responsible for the condition of a property, which is the host's.
terms.liability.p2: Nothing here limits any right you have under the consumer law of the country you are in, which stands whatever this page says.
cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.lead: Which cookies PALTAS sets, what each is for, and how to control them.
cookies.what.title: What a cookie is here
cookies.what.p1: A small piece of text stored by your browser, sent back to us on each request. We use them for a short list of things and no more.
cookies.what.p2: We set no advertising cookies and no third-party tracking cookies. There is nothing here to opt out of for that reason, because there is nothing doing it.
cookies.which.title: Which ones we set
cookies.which.p1: A session cookie when you sign in. It is httpOnly, so no script can read it, and it is what keeps you signed in between pages. Signing out destroys it.
cookies.which.p2: A language cookie and a country cookie, holding the choices you made. These are readable by the page, because the switcher in the header needs to know what is currently selected — a language preference is not a secret.
cookies.which.p3: Stripe sets its own cookies on the payment step, for fraud prevention on the card transaction. Those are Stripe's and are covered by Stripe's own policy.
cookies.control.title: Controlling them
cookies.control.p1: Your browser can block or clear all of them. Blocking the session cookie means you cannot stay signed in, so booking will not work; blocking the language cookie means the site forgets your language between visits.
cookies.control.p2: Signing out removes the session cookie immediately, on every device where that session was open.
